title: The Role of Hydrogen Sulfide in the Localization and Structural-Functional Organization of p53 Following Traumatic Brain Injury: Development of a YOLO Model for Detection and Quantification of Apoptotic Nuclei.
authors: Kirichenko, Evgeniya; Bachurin, Stanislav; Lisovin, Anton; Nabiullina, Rozaliia; Kaplya, Marya; Romanov, Aleksandr; Nwosu, Chizaram; Rodkin, Stanislav
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脑外伤后H2S对p53定位与凋亡的影响，并用YOLO检测凋亡核，虽涉及p53转录因子和分子动力学，但核心是细胞凋亡表型与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法上仅YOLO检测和简单MD，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a cascade of molecular and cellular disturbances, including apoptosis, inflammation, and destabilization of neuronal connections. The transcription factor p53 plays a pivotal role in regulating cell fate following brain injury by initiating pro-apoptotic signaling cascades. Hydrogen sulfide (H(2)S) may significantly contribute to the regulation of p53. Using scanning laser confocal microscopy, we found that after TBI, p53 accumulates extensively in the damaged cerebral cortex, showing distinct subcellular localization in neurons and astrocytes. In neurons, p53 predominantly localizes to the cytoplasm, suggesting involvement in mitochondria-dependent apoptosis, whereas in astrocytes, p53 is found in both the nucleus and cytoplasm, indicating possible activation of transcription-dependent apoptotic pathways. Quantitative analysis confirmed a correlation between p53 localization and morphological signs of cell death, as revealed by Sytox Green and Hoechst nuclear staining. Modulating H(2)S levels exerted a marked influence on p53 expression and distribution. Administration of the H(2)S donor sodium thiosulfate (Na(2)S(2)O(3)) reduced the overall number of p53-positive cells, decreased nuclear localization, and lowered the level of apoptosis. Conversely, inhibition of H(2)S synthesis using aminooxyacetic acid (AOAA) led to enhanced p53 expression, increased numbers of cells exhibiting nuclear fragmentation, and a more pronounced apoptotic response. These findings highlight a neuroprotective role for H(2)S, likely mediated through the suppression of p53-dependent cell death pathways. To improve analytical accuracy, we developed a YOLO-based deep-learning model for the automated detection of fragmented nuclei. Additionally, evolutionary and molecular dynamics analysis revealed a high degree of p53 conservation among vertebrates and indicated that, although H(2)S does not form stable complexes with p53, it may modulate its conformational dynamics.
abstract_zh: 创伤性脑损伤（TBI）触发一系列分子和细胞紊乱，包括凋亡、炎症以及神经元连接的失稳。转录因子p53在脑损伤后通过启动促凋亡信号级联反应，在调控细胞命运中发挥关键作用。硫化氢（H(2)S）可能显著参与p53的调控。利用扫描激光共聚焦显微镜，我们发现TBI后，p53在受损大脑皮层中广泛积累，在神经元和星形胶质细胞中显示出不同的亚细胞定位。在神经元中，p53主要定位于细胞质，提示其参与线粒体依赖性凋亡，而在星形胶质细胞中，p53存在于细胞核和细胞质中，表明可能激活转录依赖性凋亡通路。定量分析证实了p53定位与细胞死亡形态学标志之间的相关性，这通过Sytox Green和Hoechst核染色揭示。调节H(2)S水平对p53表达和分布产生显著影响。给予H(2)S供体硫代硫酸钠（Na(2)S(2)O(3)）减少了p53阳性细胞的总数，降低了核定位，并降低了凋亡水平。相反，使用氨基氧乙酸（AOAA）抑制H(2)S合成导致p53表达增强，核碎片细胞数量增加，以及更明显的凋亡反应。这些发现突显了H(2)S的神经保护作用，可能通过抑制p53依赖性细胞死亡通路介导。为提高分析准确性，我们开发了一种基于YOLO的深度学习模型，用于自动检测碎片化细胞核。此外，进化和分子动力学分析揭示了p53在脊椎动物中的高度保守性，并表明，尽管H(2)S不与p53形成稳定复合物，但它可能调节其构象动力学。
